violation_type.title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(C))
violation_type.short_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior
violation_type.typical_finding: A caregiver was observed at inspection communicating to the children in a manner that does not promote positive guidance and praise.

finding_variants.text: A caregiver was observed at inspection communicating to the children in a manner that does not promote positive guidance and praise.
Based on interviews with a caregiver and a parent witness, a caregiver was observed hitting a young child to redirect the young child's behavior.
Based on information provided from a DFPS investigation it was determined that a caregiver did not utilize positive statements when redirecting a child in care to move to another area in the room.
Based on the information obtained, there is enough evidence to determined that a caregiver inappropriately disciplined a child in care.
It was determined during the investigation that a caregiver did not use positive methods of discipline when they did not appropriately redirect behavior.
It was discovered during an investigation that a staff had pointed at a child and told them to sit down.

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Discipline and guidance methods were not used to encourage self-control or self-direction.  Behavior was not verbally redirected, instead, the caregiver held the child in a manner where his movements were restricted.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: During the investigation, it was determined that a caregiver did not positively redirect a child's behavior by responding to the child by asking if the child would like the caregiver to pull their hair.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on the information received from a DFPS investigation, there is sufficient evidence to support that a caregiver did not use appropriate methods of discipline such as redirecting the child's behavior.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was evaluated in regard to an investigation and a violation was found. A caregiver was pulling a child by the arm and another child by the legs to move them to a different space on the carpet instead of using positive redirection.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: One caregiver was observed on video camera speaking negatively to a group of children.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on information gathered during this investigation, a caregiver did not positively redirect a child's behavior by throwing a toy at a child.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was reviewed as part of an investigation and found non-compliant based on information obtained.    It was discovered that a caregiver was not using positive methods to redirect children due to their behaviors.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was evaluated in regard to an investigation and a violation was found. A caregiver grabbed a child and place them on their nap mat in an abrupt manner instead of using positive words to redirect the child's behavior.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on video footage, a caregiver did not use positive methods of redirecting children's behavior when she is seen picking up a child, bringing the child to the carpet, and making the child sit down. In addition, she is seen aggressively moving two children who were already sitting on the carpet.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Video footage showed a caregiver failing to implement positive redirection strategies with the children.  Video footage shows that the caregiver failed to appropriately intervene and redirect children during an altercation.  The footage shows the caregiver physically restraining one child by the arm while instructing the other child to retaliate by hitting the child.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A staff member at the operation did not use a positive form of discipline when they were directing a child to get to their place in line. The staff member told the child that they were going to "string them up" if they did not do what they were told.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was overheard telling children to stop, get on red, that's what happens, should have been listening, and go sit down to correct the behaviors of the children in the class.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was evaluated as part of a DFPS investigation and was found to be deficient. A caregiver did not use positive methods of discipline when guiding a child to sit in a chair.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: During the investigation it was found that a caregiver redirected behavior by physically holding a child's arms to pick up items for cleanup.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was observed pinching a child ear as method of redirection.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on information provided from a DFPS investigation it was determined that a caregiver did not utilize positive statements when redirecting a child in care to move to another area in the room.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: It was determined during the investigation that a caregiver did not use positive methods of discipline when they did not appropriately redirect behavior.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was redirecting a child while not using positive statements.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Video footage was observed of a child with behavioral challenges being re-directed by staff who were not using positive statements.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on information gathered during a DFPS investigation, it was determined that a caregiver did not use a positive method of redirecting a child by lifting a toddler from the floor by their wrist with one hand.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: It was discovered during an investigation that a staff had pointed at a child and told them to sit down.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on the DFPS investigation, a caregiver did not use appropriate redirection as the caregiver grabbed a child by the wrist and lifted the child from a seated position to direct the child to the sink.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was heard on video footage telling a child in a threatening tone to be quiet.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was heard raising their voice at children and did not use positive statements towards redirecting children.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation by the Department of Family and Protective Services and was found to be deficient. A caregiver attempted to manage a child's behavior through physical intervention rather than using encouraging, constructive methods. The action lacked the positive guidance strategies that help build a child?s confidence and ability to self-regulate.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver inappropriately redirected a child by picking the child up by their forearm to get the child down from climbing on a table.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Children in the younger toddler classroom were observed riding toys bicycles around the classroom and on top of mats while other children were sleeping. While the children were riding bikes, no caregiver redirected or intervened the behavior and allowed the children to continue riding the bikes in the classroom and on children's mats.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: At time of inspection a toddler caregiver did not redirect a child with positive statements when child was not following instructions.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was evaluated in regard to a DFPS investigation and compliance was not met. A caregiver did not attempt to redirect a child who was misbehaving.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on interviews with a caregiver and a parent witness, a caregiver was observed hitting a young child to redirect the young child's behavior.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on a video, a caregiver did not use positive methods to redirect a young child's behavior but instead the caregiver grabbed and a pulled a young child to cease the young child's behavior.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: The caregiver inappropriately redirects the child by pushing the victim head down to complete a task after using the restroom.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: The investigation found that a caregiver was not using positive redirection when she threatened to throw away a child's toy.
Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Positive methods of discipline and guidance were being used to redirect negative behavior.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on the information gathered during the investigation, the operation will be cited due to a caregiver not using positive methods of discipline and guidance towards a child in care.

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was evaluated during the investigation and was found to be deficient. Positive methods of discipline and guidance were not used during an occurrence of a child needing redirection.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on information obtained during an investigation, it was determined that a caregiver did not use a positive method of redirection to address undesired behavior. A caregiver re-directed a child by picking the child up by the arms in order to move them from one area of the classroom to sit them down in a chair.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: A caregiver was observed at inspection communicating to the children in a manner that does not promote positive guidance and praise.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, it was established that both the caregiver and the child's parents were cognizant of the child's history of dropping weight.  The caregiver should have guided the child in a different manner to prevent the occurrence of nursemaid's elbow.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: The standard was evaluated with regards to a standard investigation and was found not in compliance the Minimum Standards for Licensed Childcare Centers.   Based on interviews with staff, a caregiver in the 3 to 5 years old class did not use positive statements to redirect a child's behavior but instead the caregiver placed the child outside of the classroom with the door closed.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on evidence obtained during a DFPS investigation, a caregiver inappropriately re-directed children in care by grabbing them by the arm or elbow area in an attempt to lead the children to where they needed to go. A caregiver grabbed a child by the arm while the child was in a seated position and attempted to re-direct the child, making the child cry.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on the video footage on 9.19.23 a caregiver was observed lifting a child by their forearm, pulling a child off the table by their leg when redirecting.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation it was determined that caregivers at the operation were not redirecting children with positive statements. Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: As a result of an investigation it was determined that this standard is deficient. A caregiver did not use appropriate redirection with a child when the child moved into an area behind the table where they were not supposed to be.

Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior: This standard was reviewed in relation to the reported allegations and found to be deficient.
